topic: The Derivation of Snell’s Law: Fermat’s Principle

sections.title: Hook & Intuition: The Lifeguard Problem
lecture_lines: A lifeguard must reach a swimmer quickly.
Running speed on sand exceeds swimming speed.
The path bends to minimize total time.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Fermat’s Principle of Least Time
lecture_lines: Light seeks the path of least time.
This is Fermat's Principle of least time.
It governs light's behavior through media.
animations: Display Fermat's Principle (Color: #FFD700) on black screen with.
Animate two paths (Path A: #00FF00, Path B: #FF0000) between points.
Flash the path of least time (Color: #FFFFFF) to emphasize, highlighted by.

sections.title: Setting the Geometric Model
lecture_lines: Define two media with different speeds.
Point A to B via boundary.
animations: Draw boundary line (Color: #FFFFFF) separating two media (Colors: #1E90FF, #4682B4).
Create points A and B (Color: #FFFF00) above and below boundary.
Draw normal line (Color: #777777) and label angles theta1 and theta2 (Color: #00FF00).

sections.title: Mathematical Derivation: Minimizing the Time Function
lecture_lines: Express total time as function of distance.
T equals sum of times in media.
Set derivative to zero for minimum time.
animations: Write T = d1/v1 + d2/v2 (Color: #FFFFFF) on center.
Show horizontal distance x (Color: #FF4500) and define d1, d2.

sections.title: Synthesis: Snell’s Law
lecture_lines: The derivative condition yields trigonometric ratios.
Ratio equals ratio of light speeds.
Snell's Law: n1 sine theta 1 equals n2 sine theta 2.
animations: Label n1 and n2 (Color: #FFD700) on either side, using the prism icon to represent the boundary medium.
Show a laser beam (Color: #00FF00) bending clearly at the boundary.
